issues.issue: The printed label is just 'Taxes'. Recording it as property tax is defensible: the statement of activities (p2) lists only 'Property taxes' as a tax, and the budget schedules show only property tax plus zero pro-rate. But the report never breaks down this exact line, so it is an assumption.

Mixed line (grants plus other). The source of the grants (government or private) isn't stated, so no dominant category can be picked from the page. 'other' with review is defensible, but this is 47% of revenue in 'other'.

issues.on_page: Event center 2,569,557 (statement of activities p2: 'Social, cultural, and rec services')
issues.issue: Agricultural society events would normally be agriculture/fair under the entity-type rules. culture/recreation matches the p2 function label, so this is a judgment call.

issues.on_page: Debt service: General Fund 813,150 (positive inflow), Special Revenue (1,412,900), Debt Service JPA (550,000); Total (1,149,750)
issues.issue: The Total column nets a positive 813,150 General Fund inflow (possibly loan proceeds or a reclassification) against the payments. The amount matches the Total column, but recording the net as a principal payment may understate both debt proceeds and principal paid. The extraction has no decision_needed entry for this.

issues.on_page: Transfers in/(out): General 127,544, Capital Projects (1,169,676), Special Revenue 1,189,776, Debt Service (147,644); Total -
issues.issue: Transfers net to 0 in the Total column, so null is consistent with it. Gross transfers in/out of 1,317,320 aren't recorded. The JPA budget schedule (p6) shows Transfers out '-' while the GAAP statement shows JPA (147,644). These are basis differences, not spending lines.
Sales tax collected and owed to the state could be 'due to other governments'

issues.on_page: Operating expenses 6,658,461 (General Fund budget schedule, no function)
issues.issue: The entity-type rule says Operating Expenses with no function take the entity's function (agricultural society -> agriculture/fair). general government follows the GAAP label of the fund's main function, so this is a judgment call.
85% of the General Fund budget-schedule revenue is in other/miscellaneous revenue. It isn't itemized on the page, so this is defensible with review (it is likely fair/event and charges revenue).
